name: Genu Varum in Children
definition: Bow-leg alignment in children, commonly physiologic in toddlers but pathological when progressive, asymmetric or associated with metabolic/growth disorders.

investigations.principle: Standing radiographs are used when deformity is persistent, asymmetric or suspicious.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, physeal, occult injury, deformity or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Pathological deformity requires cause-specific pediatric orthopedic treatment.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Jangha/Janu alignment phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Bow-leg alignment in children, commonly physiologic in toddlers but pathological when progressive, asymmetric or associated with metabolic/growth disorders.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, open injury, severe deformity, rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, suspected infection or other listed red flags.
